teach.narration: The factor pairs are one and eighteen, two and nine, and three and six. Eighteen is above the limit, so leave it out.

teach.title: Keep only the common members
teach.narration: An intersection keeps a number only if it is in both sets. Two and three are the only shared numbers.

steps.title: Substitute three for n
steps.narration: Both occurrences of n must be replaced by three to calculate the third term.

steps.title: Substitute four for n
steps.narration: Both occurrences of n must now be replaced by four.

steps.title: Add the two terms
steps.narration: Adding a negative twelve takes us twelve lower than negative thirteen. The sum is negative twenty-five.

teach.title: Find the third term
teach.narration: Three squared is nine and six threes make eighteen. Subtract eighteen and then four.

teach.title: Substitute four for n
teach.narration: Both occurrences of n must now be replaced by four.

teach.title: Find the fourth term

steps.title: Write the identity matrix
steps.narration: An identity matrix has ones on the main diagonal and zeroes everywhere else.

steps.title: Keep the first minor
steps.narration: The top-left entry has a positive cofactor sign. Delete its row and column to get the smaller determinant.

steps.title: Find the determinant
steps.narration: The bracket is one minus zero, so the determinant of the identity matrix is one.

steps.title: Read the parallel lines
steps.narration: The arrow marks show that QR and TU are parallel. The diagram gives eighty degrees at Q and ninety-five degrees at S.

steps.title: Draw a horizontal ray SX to the right
steps.narration: Draw the ray through S. Corresponding angles made by the transversal PS with QR and SX are equal, so angle PSX is eighty degrees.

steps.title: Find the angle below the new ray
steps.narration: Ray SX splits the ninety-five-degree angle at S. Subtract the eighty-degree part above SX to find the part below it.

steps.title: Use alternate interior angles
steps.narration: SU crosses the parallel lines SX and TU. The alternate interior angles XSU and SUT are equal, so SUT is fifteen degrees.

teach.title: Use alternate interior angles
teach.narration: SU crosses the parallel lines SX and TU. The alternate interior angles XSU and SUT are equal, so SUT is fifteen degrees.

steps.title: Use the sector area formula
steps.narration: A sector covers the same fraction of the circle's area as its central angle does of a full turn.

steps.title: Put the numbers into the formula
steps.narration: Divide the angle by the full turn, then multiply by pi times the radius squared.

steps.title: Find the area of the sector
steps.narration: One hundred and forty-four divided by twelve gives twelve. Multiply by five to get sixty pi square centimetres.

teach.title: Reduce the fraction and square the radius

steps.title: Find the acute reference angle
steps.narration: One hundred and thirty-five degrees is in the second quadrant. Subtract it from one hundred and eighty degrees to get forty-five degrees.

steps.title: Use an equal-legged right triangle
steps.narration: Take both legs to be one. Pythagoras gives the hypotenuse as the square root of two, so cosine is one over that length.

steps.title: Apply the negative sign
steps.narration: Give the forty-five-degree cosine the second-quadrant sign. The result is negative square root of two over two.

steps.title: Recover the sum from the mean
steps.narration: The mean is the sum divided by how many values there are. Multiply by the count to get the sum back.

steps.title: Find the sum of seven numbers
steps.narration: The seven numbers average ninety-six, so together they add up to six hundred and seventy-two.

steps.title: Find the sum of eight numbers
steps.narration: Eight times one hundred and twelve is eight hundred and ninety-six.

steps.title: Find the eighth number
steps.narration: Eight hundred and ninety-six minus six hundred and seventy-two gives two hundred and twenty-four.

teach.title: Use the new count and mean
teach.narration: There are now eight numbers, and their mean is one hundred and twelve. Use both new values.

teach.title: Find the sum of eight numbers
teach.narration: Eight times one hundred and twelve is eight hundred and ninety-six.

teach.title: Subtract the original sum
teach.narration: The first seven numbers are still included, so the difference between the two totals is exactly the added number.

teach.title: Find the eighth number
teach.narration: Eight hundred and ninety-six minus six hundred and seventy-two gives two hundred and twenty-four.

steps.title: Divide out identical arrangements
steps.narration: Eight factorial treats every letter as different. Swapping the three identical Ts makes no new arrangement, so divide by three factorial.

steps.title: Evaluate the factorials
steps.narration: Eight factorial is forty thousand three hundred and twenty, and three times two times one is six.

steps.title: Find the distinct arrangements
steps.narration: Dividing forty thousand three hundred and twenty by six gives six thousand seven hundred and twenty distinct arrangements.

teach.title: Count the letters and repeats
teach.narration: There are eight positions to fill. T occurs three times, and each other letter occurs once.

teach.narration: Each distinct word arrangement accounts for six arrangements when the Ts are treated as different. The product gives the original total.

teach.title: Find the distinct arrangements

steps.title: Find the highest power of three
steps.narration: Twenty-seven is exactly three cubed, so the leftmost nonzero digit belongs in the twenty-sevens place.

steps.title: Fill the remaining places with zeros
steps.narration: There are no nines, threes or ones left. Write zero in each of those places.

steps.title: Write the digits in base three
steps.narration: Read the digits from biggest place to smallest. The result is one zero zero zero in base three.

teach.title: Take one group of twenty-seven

teach.title: Fill the remaining places with zeros
teach.narration: There are no nines, threes or ones left. Write zero in each of those places.

teach.title: Convert back to base ten
teach.narration: Multiplying the four digits by their place values returns twenty-seven, so the digits are correct.

teach.title: Write the digits in base three
teach.narration: Read the digits from biggest place to smallest. The result is one zero zero zero in base three.

steps.title: Match forty to the largest ratio
steps.narration: Five is the largest of the ratio numbers, so the forty apples represent five equal parts.

steps.title: Find the size of one part
steps.narration: Forty shared equally into five parts gives eight apples per part.

steps.title: Find the smallest share
steps.narration: Two groups of eight give sixteen apples.

teach.title: Use two equal parts
teach.narration: Two is the smallest ratio number, so the smallest share contains two groups of eight apples.

teach.title: Find the smallest share
teach.narration: Two groups of eight give sixteen apples.

steps.title: Use the simple interest formula
steps.narration: Simple interest is calculated on the original principal. Multiply principal, annual percentage rate and years, then divide by one hundred.

steps.title: Put the values into the formula
steps.narration: Use eight for the percentage rate because the formula already divides by one hundred.

steps.title: Divide both sides by two hundred and forty
steps.narration: The yearly interest is the coefficient of T. Divide both sides by that amount to find the time.

steps.title: State the time in years
steps.narration: Five halves makes two whole years and half a year, so the time is two and a half years.

teach.narration: The yearly interest is the coefficient of T. Divide both sides by that amount to find the time.

steps.title: Write the variation equation
steps.narration: Joint variation puts both m and u in the numerator. Inverse variation puts q in the denominator. The same constant k applies each time.

steps.title: Reduce the constant
steps.narration: Four and six share a factor of two. Cancelling it gives two thirds.

steps.title: Substitute the second set of values
steps.narration: Use the same constant with six and four in the numerator and eight fifths as the divisor.

steps.title: Evaluate the new value of p
steps.narration: Sixteen divided by eight is two. Multiply by five to get ten.

teach.title: Write the variation equation
teach.narration: Joint variation puts both m and u in the numerator. Inverse variation puts q in the denominator. The same constant k applies each time.

teach.title: Use the known value of p
teach.narration: Substitute three, two and one for m, u and q, then set the result equal to four.

teach.title: Multiply the known factors
teach.narration: The numerator contains three times two, which is six. Dividing by one leaves six times k.

teach.title: Divide both sides by six
teach.narration: Divide both sides by six to leave the constant k on its own.

teach.title: Reduce the constant
teach.narration: Four and six share a factor of two. Cancelling it gives two thirds.

teach.title: Substitute the second set of values
teach.narration: Use the same constant with six and four in the numerator and eight fifths as the divisor.

teach.title: Multiply by the reciprocal
teach.narration: Two thirds of six is four, and four times four is sixteen. Dividing by eight fifths means multiplying by five eighths.

teach.title: Evaluate the new value of p
teach.narration: Sixteen divided by eight is two. Multiply by five to get ten.
